transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-30 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Rahul Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Product), Mark Rivers (Glenwood CTO), Sophie Tang (Head of Platform), Ethan Yu (Security), Priya Nair (ML Eng)

[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off in a second, looks like most folks are here. I'm Jamie, I'm the AE for Glenwood, and with me is Rahul, our solutions engineer, and Lena from product.
[00:18] Mark Rivers: Hey Jamie, hey team. Thanks, appreciate the time. First time with Redwood, so excited to see the JSON mode stuff.
[00:24] Sophie Tang: Yes hi, gonna be fairly practical — we're mainly interested in how schema enforcement helps us keep outputs structured for downstream pipelines.
[00:36] Rahul Kapoor: Great. Today's agenda — quick recap of goals, live console sandbox demo focusing on schema-first tool invocations (JSON mode), then VPC/pilot ops and security deep dive with Ethan. We'll leave time for Q&A and next steps.
[00:50] Priya Nair: Quick ask — can we test with our existing reranker + embedding flow? We want to see how Redwood handles typed outputs feeding into our retriever.
[01:05] Rahul Kapoor: Absolutely, we'll show an example where the model returns a typed order JSON that flows into a downstream search call. Note: in the sandbox we can wire up mock tools to simulate your reranker.
[01:20] Lena Ortiz: I'll chime in on guardrails — JSON mode plus response contracts can prevent hallucinated fields and enforce enums for critical fields like payment_method.
[01:34] [02:00] Screen share starts (console)
[02:12] Rahul Kapoor: OK this is the Redwood Console sandbox tenant. On the left you can see the JSON Mode toggle — when enabled you supply a schema (we have a sample order schema preloaded). You can also attach a tool-binding: the 'create_order' tool here expects order_id, items[], total, customer_id.
[02:45] Sophie Tang: That schema looks strict, what happens if the model returns an extra field or a misspelled key?
[02:58] Rahul Kapoor: Good question — by default the runtime validates and rejects responses that don't match. You can choose a 'coerce' mode that tries to map keys, or a 'reject+fallback' policy that falls back to a smaller, faster model or a cached response.
[03:20] Mark Rivers: Is that in-hosted only or will it apply to private deployments in our VPC?
[03:28] Rahul Kapoor: It applies across hosted, Dedicated, and Private — the enforcement is in the runtime layer that we ship with the control plane. In Private deployments the same JSON-mode runtime runs in your VPC with local policy controls.
[03:45] [04:00] Lena Ortiz: For the sandbox demo I uploaded a prompt set that includes edge cases — missing addresses, ambiguous sku codes — so you can see the validation triggers.
[04:18] [05:00] Live invocation: model => typed JSON response
[05:12] Rahul Kapoor: Here's an invocation — the model returned a payload but notice the 'shipping_address' came back as a string instead of the structured object. Because policy is 'reject+fallback', the runtime logged the mismatch and re-invoked a fallback policy which returned an alternate, validated response.
[05:45] Priya Nair: Filtration — can we see the logs? We need to map why it failed.
[05:52] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, tracing shows the validation error and token-level latency. You can also export the full audit log (we'll show security later).
[06:12] [07:00] Sophie Tang: About the tool call — we need to call our internal order API, which is inside our VPC. How does Redwood invoke that?
[07:18] Rahul Kapoor: For Private VPCs we support a connector that you deploy (small agent) which accepts signed, authenticated calls from the Redwood runtime over your private network. You control a whitelist and can enforce mTLS. We also support a proxy pattern where the runtime sends events to an SQS/SNS topic you own.
[07:42] Ethan Yu: On authentication — what about KMS? We need customer-managed keys/HSM for secrets and model context encryption.
[07:52] Rahul Kapoor: We support KMS integrations: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via PKCS11. For Private installs, keys never leave your key domain — we can integrate with your HSM. We'll include the security integration guide.
[08:15] [09:00] Jamie Chen: Quick tangent — cost/latency tradeoffs. If you enforce strict schema validation and use retries/fallbacks, there are extra token costs sometimes. Our Optimize tool will analyze prompt sets and recommend batching and caching rules to reduce re-invocations and prefix tokens.
[09:30] Mark Rivers: Do you have any numbers? e.g., 95th latency and per-invocation token delta with a reject+fallback policy?
[09:42] Rahul Kapoor: Ballpark: with a fallback to a small 3B variant you might add 40–120ms, and token cost for the extra recheck could be 10–40 tokens depending on prompt length. But Optimize can recommend caching common prefixes so the delta gets minimal. We can run a micro-benchmark during the pilot.
[10:10] [11:00] Demo: schema-driven tool chaining
[11:20] Rahul Kapoor: Now I'm wiring a tool-binding: model returns order JSON, runtime maps fields into a tool invocation, we have a 'validate_address' tool (mocked) then 'create_order' tool. Notice the console enforces schemas between steps so malformed address fails early.
[11:45] Priya Nair: Nice — can we write custom transform hooks if we need to normalize sku formats?
[11:52] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, the runtime supports lightweight transform functions (javascript or WASM) that run as part of the pipeline. For Private we can run them in your environment.
[12:18] [13:00] Sophie Tang: What about rollout policies? We want canarying for new schema changes; our platform team wants traffic splits by percentage, and auto rollback on error spikes.
[13:28] Lena Ortiz: Rollouts are built-in — you declare a schema version, a rollout policy (percentages, health checks), and automatic fallback to previous schema/model if error rate exceeds threshold. You can also set SLOs by endpoint.
[13:50] Mark Rivers: How are errors surfaced? We need clear tracing tied to the original request so we can replay.
[13:58] Rahul Kapoor: Each request gets a trace id. The console stores token-level traces, validation failures, model variant used, and tool invocation logs. You can stream or export those to your observability stack.
[14:20] [15:00] Security deep-dive with Ethan
[15:10] Ethan Yu: From compliance side, we need SOC 2 type 2, audit logs retention policy, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and DLP on training data. Also curious about data residency in EU.
[15:30] Rahul Kapoor: We are SOC 2 compliant for hosted. For Private deployments we provide the control plane for your team to host in-region. Audit logs are configurable — retention to 7, 30, 90+ days and export to your S3. SSO via SAML/OIDC with SCIM. We also have redaction hooks in the runtime and can integrate with your DLP.
[15:58] Ethan Yu: Does Redwood store any customer prompts or model outputs in hosted?
[16:06] Jamie Chen: By default hosted retains metadata for billing, but full text retention is configurable per-customer. For customers with strict retention we recommend Private or Dedicated and we'll disable storage of prompt/response content.
[16:28] [17:00] Priya Nair: A small nit — in the console, the runtime validation showed 'K-V cash' in the trace instead of 'KV cache', maybe the transcriber is off, but do you support persistent KV caches for chat?
[17:12] Rahul Kapoor: Haha yeah the tokenizer sometimes hears that. We do support persistent KV caches for session acceleration; for Private those caches can be pinned to your local SSDs and persisted across restarts.
[17:30] [18:00] Live: hooking customer mock API via VPC connector
[18:10] Rahul Kapoor: Here I'm configuring a connector and mapping the authorization header to a signed token. For real pilots we generate short-lived credentials that your agent redeems.
[18:35] Sophie Tang: Can the connector perform data filters to redact PII before leaving the VPC?
[18:42] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, you can run transforms and redaction rules inside the connector; since it runs in your network those rules are under your control.
[19:00] [20:00] Discussion: pilot scope and success metrics
[20:12] Jamie Chen: Proposed pilot: 4-week sandbox -> ingest 2k prompt/response pairs, run 3 micro-benchmarks for latency/cost, validate schema enforcement on 5 production endpoints, and run an ops readiness checklist for VPC deployment.
[20:35] Mark Rivers: Sounds reasonable. Our success metrics: <200ms p50 for critical endpoints, <5% schema rejection rate (after fixes), and clear audit logs exported to our SIEM.
[20:52] Jamie Chen: We'll include that in the runbook. Priya, you'll get the sandbox access and a guide to wire your reranker.
[21:08] Priya Nair: Thanks, also want to test conversational state and KV eviction policies.
[21:16] Rahul Kapoor: We'll include a KV eviction scenario in the test plan.
[21:35] [22:00] Pricing and commitment chat
[22:10] Jamie Chen: For pilots we offer a sandbox tier with limited compute credits; if you move to Private pilot we'll provide an estimated one-month infra cost for the VPC agent and expected GPU footprint based on your throughput. Dedicated reserved capacity estimate is separate.
[22:38] Mark Rivers: Any minimums for Private?
[22:44] Jamie Chen: No hard minimum for the pilot, but production Private typically has a monthly platform fee and minimum committed throughput for GPU pools. We'll send a pricing sheet.
[23:00] [24:00] Q&A rapid fire
[24:12] Ethan Yu: Can we run a crypto review on your connector code?
[24:18] Rahul Kapoor: Yes we'll provide the connector repo or an SBOM and you can run an internal review.
[24:30] Sophie Tang: Do you have any customers using this pattern for high-frequency retail ordering?
[24:36] Jamie Chen: We do — a couple of merchants use schema-first pipelines to drive order creation with low error rates. We can share anonymized case studies.
[24:50] [26:00] Slight transcription glitch — speaker label swap for a minute
[26:12] Rahul Kapoor: Back to the console — showing the runtime policy editor; you can set validation severity, fallback targets, and traffic splits per route.
[26:35] Priya Nair: For transforms you mentioned WASM — can we bring our own wasm modules?
[26:45] Rahul Kapoor: Yep. We'll sign and vet modules in hosted; in Private you can load them directly.
[27:05] [28:00] Demo: Optimize recommendations
[28:20] Lena Ortiz: This is Redwood Optimize — it analyzes your prompt corpus and suggests batching windows, prefix caching, and quantization profiles to reduce token spend without hurting quality. For example, it recommended a 32-token prefix cache for your checkout flow which reduced average token per checkout by ~12%.
[28:50] Mark Rivers: We care about cost predictability. Can Optimize give monthly cost projections?
[28:56] Lena Ortiz: It gives estimates based on usage patterns and different deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and can show tradeoffs visually.
[29:20] [30:00] Conversation: fallback strategies and monitoring
[30:12] Rahul Kapoor: Key pattern: primary model -> schema validation -> tool-binding; on validation failure you can choose: immediate reject to client, re-run with stricter prompt, fallback to a deterministic tool, or return a canned response. The choice depends on SLA. Logs capture why you chose which path.
[30:40] Ethan Yu: For auditing, we need immutable logs — are the traces tamper-evident?
[30:48] Rahul Kapoor: We support write-once export to your object store and can ship hashes to an audit ledger.
[31:15] [33:00] Customer concerns: vendor lock-in and migration
[33:12] Mark Rivers: How locked are we if we invest in Redwood-specific schemas and transform hooks?
[33:22] Lena Ortiz: Schemas are standard JSON Schema; transforms are portable if you use WASM or small JS snippets. We provide export tools for model prompts and training artifacts, and we encourage multi-cloud patterns.
[33:45] Priya Nair: Is there an SDK for local dev and testing?
[33:50] Rahul Kapoor: Yes a local dev kit that emulates the runtime so you can unit test your schema constraints and tool bindings.
[34:10] [36:00] Walkthrough of sample pilot timeline in Confluence doc
[36:20] Jamie Chen: I'm pulling up the pilot plan — week 0 onboarding, week 1 sandbox tests, week 2 micro-benchmarks, week 3 VPC connector staging, week 4 pilot wrap and recommendations.
[36:42] Sophie Tang: Can we do a mid-pilot review with eng + security?
[36:48] Jamie Chen: Yes we'll schedule a 30‑minute check-in at week 2.
[37:05] [38:00] Small back-and-forth on deployment packaging
[38:12] Rahul Kapoor: For on-prem we provide a tarball and helm charts. For VPC connector it's a tiny service (1-2 vCPU) that brokers signed requests.
[38:34] Ethan Yu: What about network egress — will any data exit without encryption?
[38:40] Rahul Kapoor: No, all control-plane comms are TLS+mTLS. Payloads in Private stay inside your network unless you opt into logging exports.
[39:00] [41:00] Customer asks for demo artifacts and templates
[41:12] Jamie Chen: We'll share the schema templates, sample prompt sets, and a runbook — link will be in the follow-up.
[41:28] Mark Rivers: Also include the SIEM export example and the KMS integration guide.
[41:34] Jamie Chen: Noted.
[42:00] [45:00] Wrap-up and recap
[45:12] Jamie Chen: Quick recap — primary deliverables: runbook + pricing, sandbox access for Priya, connector code and security guide for Ethan, and a pilot test plan. We'll also run a small benchmark once you provide sample traffic.
[45:36] Sophie Tang: Timeline works — we'll try to get the prompt set by end of week.
[45:45] Mark Rivers: Appreciate the demo. One last ask — can we have a short architecture diagram enumerating data flows for the VPC connector?
[45:55] Rahul Kapoor: We'll include that in the email.
[46:10] [50:00] Final logistics
[50:12] Jamie Chen: I'll send calendar invites for the week-2 check-in and sandbox onboarding. Expect the runbook and pricing by Tuesday.
[50:28] Priya Nair: Looking forward to hands-on with the console.
[50:34] Ethan Yu: We'll start our internal review of the connector.
[50:40] Jamie Chen: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[50:48] Mark Rivers: Thanks all.
[50:52] [52:00] Call ends

Notes: Minor transcription errors noted in places (e.g., 'K-V cash'). Shared links referenced: https://redwood.ai/pilot-scope/glenwood (pilot scope doc), https://redwood.ai/security/glenwood-connector (connector repo placeholder).

End of transcript.
